name: Short drift distance (µm)
sentence: How far proseg usually lets RNA drift from where it lies. Short: RNA mostly counts for the cell it lies in, or for none. Long: RNA near a border can count for the cell across it.
info: Made-up cells, started from cells only: 36 marker transcripts of each lie 0.5-3 µm over the border. Other settings at proseg's defaults. Each panel: the middle of 27 copies run in proseg 3.2.0. Drift starts after iteration 200, so earlier differences are chance. On real 500 µm squares, 2 µm gave 9 % fewer pink dots than 1 µm (Cellpose: 6 %), but took the cells' own RNA at the same spots just as often.
spotTip: Bigger dots: RNA lying 0.5 to 3 µm over the border from its own cell, in the colour of the cell whose count keeps it.
statTip: Bigger dots counted for their own cell, on average over every 5th iteration since drift began. As the distance grows, this cell's count keeps less of its own RNA by the border: about 77, 75 and 70 of 95.
